title: The Water Under Texas Is 10,000 Years Old and Running Out

intro_meme.prompt: A cartoon ancient wrinkled water-droplet character, looking exhausted, sipping the last bit of water from a giant straw nervously, spotlighted on a stand-up stage.

outro_meme.prompt: The same ancient wrinkled water-droplet character giving a tired thumbs up next to a glowing 'READ MORE' sign.

sources.fact: The High Plains Water District was created in 1951 to conserve the Ogallala Aquifer. About 95% of the water pumped from it goes to irrigated agriculture, and withdrawals already exceed natural recharge.
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension: daily water demand hit as high as half an inch per day during 100-plus-degree stretches this year.
